intro_notes: Scouts BSA Test Lab Pilot Badge (Valid through 2026-12-31). Physics is the science of how things move, interact, and exist, from the tiniest particles inside atoms to the vast galaxies stretching across space. It’s the foundation of modern technology, the reason rockets fly, and the explanation behind everyday phenomena like why your phone works or how a soccer ball curves through the air.

NOTE: Any registered adult Scouting America volunteer may serve as the counselor/reviewer for a Test Lab badge. Upon completion of all requirements and the official Scouting America Test Lab survey, Scouts receive an official Certificate of Completion that converts to Merit Badge credit if the badge graduates to permanent status.

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Your patrol rolls two solid spheres of the exact same size and shape down an inclined ramp from rest: one made of aluminum and one made of heavy brass. Neglecting air resistance, how do their accelerations down the ramp compare?
quiz_item.question: Your patrol rolls two solid spheres of the exact same size and shape down an inclined ramp from rest: one made of aluminum and one made of heavy brass. Neglecting air resistance, how do their accelerations down the ramp compare?
options: A. The heavier brass sphere accelerates twice as fast because it has more gravitational mass.
B. Both spheres accelerate down the ramp at the same rate because gravitational acceleration and rotational inertia scale proportionally with mass for identical solid spheres.
C. The lighter aluminum sphere reaches the bottom first because it has less friction.
D. Neither sphere rolls unless the ramp angle exceeds 45 degrees.
choices: A. The heavier brass sphere accelerates twice as fast because it has more gravitational mass.
B. Both spheres accelerate down the ramp at the same rate because gravitational acceleration and rotational inertia scale proportionally with mass for identical solid spheres.
C. The lighter aluminum sphere reaches the bottom first because it has less friction.
D. Neither sphere rolls unless the ramp angle exceeds 45 degrees.
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Both spheres accelerate down the ramp at the same rate because gravitational acceleration and rotational inertia scale proportionally with mass for identical solid spheres.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Since both gravitational force and moment of inertia are proportional to mass (I = 2/5 m r^2), mass cancels out of the equation of motion on an incline.

Theoretical Model Testing: Quantitative mathematical predictions require rigorous empirical experimental validation inside controlled laboratories.

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: What happens to energy and matter when a mechanical wave travels across the surface of a quiet pond?
quiz_item.question: What happens to energy and matter when a mechanical wave travels across the surface of a quiet pond?
options: A. Water molecules travel outward from the center all the way to the shoreline at the speed of the wave.
B. Potential energy is destroyed at each wave crest and recreated from nothing at each trough.
C. Energy travels outward across the pond while individual water molecules oscillate mostly up and down in place.
D. Gravity stops acting on the water surface until the wave vibrations completely die out.
choices: A. Water molecules travel outward from the center all the way to the shoreline at the speed of the wave.
B. Potential energy is destroyed at each wave crest and recreated from nothing at each trough.
C. Energy travels outward across the pond while individual water molecules oscillate mostly up and down in place.
D. Gravity stops acting on the water surface until the wave vibrations completely die out.
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. Energy travels outward across the pond while individual water molecules oscillate mostly up and down in place.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Waves transfer energy from one place to another without transporting the bulk matter of the medium, which simply oscillates around its resting position (p. 17).

Swing a water bucket or tray filled with water glasses to demonstrate centripetal force. (E) Option E: Balance. Explore center of gravity, inertia, and harmonic motion using a Tweety Bopper. (F) Option F: Visualize Sound. Visualize Chladni patterns using a tonoscope. (G) Option G: Cartesian Diver. Demonstrate buoyancy and the ideal gas law with Cartesian divers. quiz_item.question: In the Cartesian diver experiment, why does the diver sink to the bottom when you squeeze the sides of the sealed plastic bottle?
options: A. Squeezing the bottle heats the water, which makes the liquid less dense than the plastic diver.
B. Squeezing creates a magnetic field at the bottom of the bottle that pulls the diver downward.
C. Squeezing removes gravity from the upper half of the bottle and concentrates it at the base.
D. Increased pressure compresses the air pocket inside the diver, increasing its overall density above the density of water.

quiz_item.correct_answer: D. Increased pressure compresses the air pocket inside the diver, increasing its overall density above the density of water.
